  html_document: default

See ST Waterfall Plots for details of analysis methods.


```{r,echo=FALSE}
HtHWaterfall <- function(means.tbl, t1, t2, assessment='Yield', alpha=0.05, error = 'bootstrap', basis='Difference',baseplot=FALSE,PooledSD=NA) {
  grey = "#999999"
yellow <- "#F0E442"
blue <- "#0072B2"
vermillion <- "#D55E00"

  Mean1 = means.tbl[, t1]
  Mean2 = means.tbl[, t2]
  
  if(mean(Mean1,na.rm=TRUE)<mean(Mean2,na.rm=TRUE)) {
    tmp <- t1
    t1 <- t2
    t2 <- tmp
    tmp <- Mean1
    Mean1 <- Mean2
    Mean2 <- tmp
  }
  
  YieldChange = Mean1 - Mean2
  difference.ylab = paste(assessment,':', t1, '-' , t2)
  if(basis=='Percent') {
    YieldChange =  100 *  YieldChange / ((Mean1 + Mean2) / 2)
      difference.ylab = paste('Percent Difference, (',
                       t1,
                       '-' ,
                       t2,
                       ')/mean(',
                       t1,
                       ',',
                       t2,
                       ')',
                       sep = '')
  }
  YieldChange <- YieldChange[!is.na(YieldChange)]
  
  

  hth.main = paste('Head to Head, ', t1, 'vs' , t2,'over',length(YieldChange),'Trials')
  
  #range <- max(YieldChange)-min(YieldChange)
  #line1 <- range * .8
  #line2 <- range * .72
  #line3 <- range * .64
  #line4 <- range * .56
  #line5 <- range*0.1
  
  
  line1 <- max(YieldChange) * .9
  line2 <- max(YieldChange) * .8
  line3 <- max(YieldChange) * .7
  line4 <- max(YieldChange) * .6
  
  


  o <- order(YieldChange,
             decreasing = TRUE,
             na.last = NA)
  YieldChange <- YieldChange[o]
  df.bar <- barplot(
    YieldChange,
    col = grey,
    border = grey,
    space = 0.5,
    main = hth.main,
    ylab = difference.ylab,
    xaxt='n'
  )

 
  
  offset = quantile(df.bar,0.25)
  offset2 = quantile(df.bar,0.05)
  
  Mean = mean(YieldChange)
  Variance = var(YieldChange)
  if(is.na(PooledSD)) {
    StdDev <- sd(YieldChange)
  } else {
    StdDev <- PooledSD
  }
   # StdErr = sqrt(
  #    var(YieldChange) /
  #      length(YieldChange)
    #),
    Median = median(YieldChange)
  
  if(!is.na(PooledSD)) {
    StdDev <- PooledSD
  }
  StdErr <- StdDev/sqrt(length(YieldChange))
  
  Average.text <-
    paste('Mean =', format(Mean, 2))
  CI <-
    Mean + qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * c(-StdErr, StdErr)
  
  Average.text <- paste(Average.text,', CI=(', format(CI[1], 2), ',', format(CI[2], 2),')',sep='')
  SD.text <- paste('SD =', format(StdDev, 2))
  
   
  
  WinRate <-
    100 * sum(YieldChange > 0) / length(YieldChange)
  WinRate.text <- paste('Win Rate =', format(WinRate, 2))
  text(offset, line1, Average.text, adj = c(0, 0))
  #text(offset, line2, SD.text, adj = c(0, 0))
  #text(offset, line2, CI.text, adj = c(0, 0))
  if(baseplot) {
    text(offset, line3, WinRate.text, adj = c(0, 0))
    return(0)
  }
  
  n <- length(YieldChange)
  
  if (error == 'ecdf') {
    Win.CI <-
      WinRate + c(-100, 100) * ((1 / sqrt(
        2 * length(YieldChange)
      ) * log(2 / 0.1)))
    Win.CI[Win.CI > 100] <- 100
    Win.CI[Win.CI < 0] <- 0
    WinRate.CI.text <- paste('eCDF CI =',format(Win.CI[1],2),'-',format(Win.CI[2],2))
    #WinRate.CI.text <- 'Win Rate CI (eCDF) ='
  } else if(error == 'normal') {
    se.p <- 100*sqrt(((WinRate/100)*(1-WinRate/100))/length(YieldChange))
   # WinRate <- 100*(1-pnorm(0,Mean,StdDev))
   # WinRate.text <- paste('Win Rate (approx) =',format(WinRate,2))
    Win.CI <- WinRate + qnorm(1-alpha/2)*c(-se.p,se.p)
    WinRate.CI.text <- paste('Normal Approx. CI =',format(Win.CI[1],2),'-',format(Win.CI[2],2))

    #WinRate.text <- 'Win Rate (approx) ='
  } else if (error=='nonpar') {
    boot.samples <- 1000
    boots <- rep(0, 1000)
    
    for (i in 1:boot.samples) {
      obs <- sample(YieldChange, replace = TRUE)
      boots[i] <- 100 * sum(obs > 0) / n 
    }
      Win.CI <- quantile(boots,c(alpha/2,1-alpha/2))
      WinRate.CI.text <- paste('Bootstrap percentile CI =',format(Win.CI[1],2),'-',format(Win.CI[2],2))
  } else {
    boot.samples <- 1000
    boots <- rep(0, 1000)
     WinRate <- 100*(1-pnorm(0,Mean,StdDev))
     WinRate.text <- paste('Win Rate (approx) =',format(WinRate,2))
    for (i in 1:boot.samples) {
      obs <- sample(YieldChange, replace = TRUE)
      sample.mean <- mean(obs)
      sample.sd <- sd(obs)
      boots[i] <- 100*(1 - pnorm(0, sample.mean, sample.sd))-WinRate
    }
      boot.se <- sd(boots)
      Win.CI <- WinRate + qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * c(-boot.se, boot.se)
      WinRate.CI.text <-
        paste(
          'Parameteric Boostrap CI  =',
          format(Win.CI[1], 2),
          '-',
          format(Win.CI[2], 2)
        )
  }
  text(offset, line3, WinRate.text, adj = c(0, 0))
  text(offset, line4, WinRate.CI.text, adj = c(0, 0))
  
  y0 = max(YieldChange) * .1

  bar.width <- max(df.bar)-min(df.bar)
  
  lower <- min(df.bar)+bar.width*(Win.CI[1]/100)
  if(lower<min(df.bar)) lower = min(df.bar)
    
  upper <- min(df.bar)+bar.width*(Win.CI[2]/100)
  if(upper>max(df.bar)) upper = max(df.bar)

  mid <- min(df.bar)+bar.width*(WinRate/100)
  fifty <- (max(df.bar)+min(df.bar))/2
  segments(x0=upper, y0=y0, y1 = -y0, col = vermillion,lwd=2)
  segments(x0=lower, y0=y0, y1 = -y0, col = vermillion,lwd=2)
  segments(x0=mid, y0=2*y0, y1 = -2*y0, col = blue,lwd=3)
  segments(x0=fifty, y0=y0*.7, y1 = -y0*.7, col = yellow,lwd=3)
  
  sw <- shapiro.test(YieldChange)
  text(offset, line2, paste('Shapiro-Wilks p-value =',format(sw$p.value,2)), adj = c(0, 0))
}
```

# META data

```{r}
means <- read.delim("./META/trialTable.SmyCol1.tab",header=FALSE)
trt.means <- colMeans(means,na.rm=TRUE)

best <- which(rank(trt.means)==max(rank(trt.means)))
second <- which(rank(trt.means)==max(rank(trt.means))-1)
worst <- which(rank(trt.means)==min(rank(trt.means)))
```


## Best vs Second best

We show the nonparametric CI side-by-side with the normal approximation CI. Since Shapiro-Wilks is not-significant, the normal approximation is appropriate and more efficient.

```{r,fig.width=12,fig.height=5}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
HtHWaterfall(means,best,second, error='nonpar',basis='Difference')
HtHWaterfall(means,best,second, error='normal',basis='Difference')
```

The CI contains 50%, so we cannot claim that one variety outperforms the other consistently.

## Best vs Worst
```{r,fig.width=12,fig.height=5}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
HtHWaterfall(means,best,worst, error='nonpar',basis='Difference')
HtHWaterfall(means,best,worst, error='normal',basis='Difference')
```

Here, we see that the best yielding variety outperforms the worst yielding variety at ~80% of the tested locations; we can infer a CI at least 70% win rate for this variety, compared to the worst. Since the data a approximately normal, there is little difference between the two methods.



# Berndt data

```{r}
means <- read.delim("./Berndt/trialTable.SmyCol3.tab",header=FALSE)
trt.means <- colMeans(means,na.rm=TRUE)

best <- which(rank(trt.means)==max(rank(trt.means)))
second <- which(rank(trt.means)==max(rank(trt.means))-1)
worst <- which(rank(trt.means)==min(rank(trt.means)))
```

In these data, the data are not normally distributed, so we would prefer the non-parametric method over the normal approximation. 

Note that the assymetry in the data is very obvious is the difference in the graphs. We have much less confidence that best out performs the second best, even though the calculated win rate is not very different. These data are Percent Control ratings, not yield data.


## Best vs Second best

```{r,fig.width=12,fig.height=5}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
HtHWaterfall(means,best,second, error='nonpar',basis='Difference')
HtHWaterfall(means,best,second, error='normal',basis='Difference')
```

## Best vs Worst

```{r,fig.width=12,fig.height=5}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
HtHWaterfall(means,best,worst, error='nonpar',basis='Difference')
HtHWaterfall(means,best,worst, error='normal',basis='Difference')
```


# Ryan Phelps data

```{r}
means <- read.delim("./Ryan Phelps/trialTable.SmyCol3.tab",header=FALSE)
trt.means <- colMeans(means,na.rm=TRUE)

best <- which(rank(trt.means)==max(rank(trt.means)))
second <- which(rank(trt.means)==max(rank(trt.means))-1)
worst <- which(rank(trt.means)==min(rank(trt.means)))
```

Again, these data are approximately normal, but not that the normal CI exceeds 100%. We could trim this, but I think it best to leave it, as a reminder that the normal CI is an approximation.

## Best vs Second best

```{r,fig.width=12,fig.height=5}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
HtHWaterfall(means,best,second, error='nonpar',basis='Difference')
HtHWaterfall(means,best,second, error='normal',basis='Difference')
```

## Best vs Worst

```{r,fig.width=12,fig.height=5}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
HtHWaterfall(means,best,worst, error='nonpar',basis='Difference')
HtHWaterfall(means,best,worst, error='normal',basis='Difference')
```
